text_blocks.snippet: Both natural immunity from a previous COVID-19 infection and immunity from vaccination offer protection against reinfection, but they differ in their duration and effectiveness. Studies indicate that natural immunity may wane faster than vaccine-induced immunity. A study published by the National Institutes of Health (NIH) found that after 9 months, the risk of reinfection was similar between those with natural immunity, vaccine-induced immunity, and those previously unexposed. However, other research suggests that vaccination provides longer-lasting protection.
